steps: Check the axes first: distance-time or speed-time?
Distance-time: the gradient is the speed; a flat line means stopped.
Speed-time: the gradient is the acceleration; the area underneath is the distance.
Match the units before dividing: turn minutes into hours.
method_card.title: How to Work with Real-Life Graphs
method_card.content:
Distance-time graphs: The gradient gives the speed. A horizontal section means the object is stationary. A steeper line means faster speed.

Speed-time graphs: The gradient gives acceleration. The area under the graph gives the distance travelled.

Conversion graphs: Straight lines that convert between units (e.g. miles ↔ km, £ ↔ €).
method_card.example:
A car travels 60 km in 1.5 hours, then stops for 30 minutes.

Speed = 60 ÷ 1.5 = 40 km/h. The graph shows a line from (0,0) to (1.5, 60) then a flat line to (2, 60).

gold.display: A speed-time graph: 0→10 m/s in 4 s, constant 10 m/s for 6 s, then 10→0 in 5 s. Find total distance.

misconceptions.message: ½(4)(10) + 6(10) + ½(5)(10) = 20 + 60 + 25 = 105 m. Forgetting the ½ on the sloped parts gives 40 + 60 + 50 = 150.

gold.hint: Split the shape into triangle, rectangle, triangle and add the three areas.

guided_steps.say: Distance is the total area. Split the trapezium into two triangles and a rectangle.

guided_steps.hint: base × height, over the 6 s at 10 m/s.

guided_steps.done: 105 m over 15 s averages 7 m/s, between 0 and 10, so it is sensible.

gold.display: A car travels at 30 m/s for 10 s then decelerates at 6 m/s². How long until it stops?

misconceptions.message: Time = speed ÷ deceleration = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 s. Multiplying (30 × 6 = 180) instead of dividing is the slip.

gold.hint: Time to stop = speed ÷ deceleration; the steady part does not matter.

guided_steps.say: The 10 s at steady speed does not affect the stopping time. Only the deceleration does.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the speed by the deceleration.

guided_steps.pre: Check: losing 6 m/s each second for 5 s loses 6 × 5 =
guided_steps.done: That is the full 30 m/s, so 5 s is right.

gold.display: A distance-time graph shows: (0,0), (2,40), (3,40), (5,100). What is the speed in the final section (km/h)?

misconceptions.message: Speed = change in distance ÷ change in time = (100 − 40) ÷ (5 − 3) = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 km/h. Dividing by the whole time 5 instead of the 2-hour section gives 12.

gold.hint: Speed is the gradient of the last section: change in distance ÷ change in time.

guided_steps.say: Speed on a distance-time graph is the gradient. Use only the final section, from t = 3 to t = 5.

guided_steps.hint: Subtract the distances at the two ends.
Divide the distance change by the time change.

guided_steps.done: That matches the 60 km climb, so 30 km/h is right.

gold.display: A speed-time graph shows a car accelerating from rest to speed v in 8 seconds. The distance travelled (the area under the graph) is 80 m. Find v.

misconceptions.message: ½ × 8 × v = 80, so 4v = 80 and v = 20 m/s. Forgetting the ½ gives 80 ÷ 8 = 10, too small.

gold.hint: The area of the triangle is ½ × base × height; set it equal to 80 and solve for v.

guided_steps.say: The distance is the area of the triangle: ½ × base × height. Here the height is the unknown speed v.

guided_steps.hint: Put v = 20 back into the area.
guided_steps.done: It gives the 80 m area, so v = 20 m/s is right.

gold.display: A car accelerates from rest at 4 m/s² for 10 seconds. What is the final speed?

misconceptions.message: Final speed = acceleration × time = 4 × 10 = 40 m/s. Dividing (10 ÷ 4 = 2.5) instead of multiplying is the slip.

gold.hint: Final speed = acceleration × time when starting from rest.

guided_steps.say: Final speed = start speed + acceleration × time. From rest means the start speed is 0.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply the acceleration by the time.
Add the gain to the start speed of 0.

guided_steps.pre: Check: gaining 4 m/s each second for 10 s gives 4 × 10 =
guided_steps.done: That is the 40 m/s, so the final speed is right.

bronze.display: The distance-time graph shows a journey. How far did the person travel in the first 2 hours?

misconceptions.message: At t = 2 hours the line sits at 60 km. Reading its final height at t = 4 gives 90 km, which is the whole journey, not the first 2 hours.

bronze.hint: The distance is the height of the line; read it at the time given.

guided_steps.say: The distance travelled is the height of the line. Read it at the time you are asked for.

guided_steps.pre: Read the height at time = 1 hour:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line up to t = 1.

guided_steps.pre: Read the height at time = 2 hours:
guided_steps.hint: Follow the line up to t = 2.

guided_steps.pre: So the distance in the first 2 hours is
guided_steps.hint: It is the height you just read at t = 2.
guided_steps.done: The graph reads 60 km at 2 hours, so that is the distance travelled.

bronze.display: Using the distance-time graph, for how long did the person stop?

misconceptions.message: The flat section runs from t = 2 to t = 3, so the stop lasts 3 − 2 = 1 hour. Writing 3 reads the end time, not the length.

bronze.hint: A stop is a flat, horizontal section; measure how long it lasts.

guided_steps.say: A stop shows up as a flat, horizontal section: the distance is not changing.

guided_steps.pre: The flat part starts at time =
guided_steps.hint: Read where the line first goes flat.

guided_steps.pre: The flat part ends at time =
guided_steps.hint: Read where the line starts climbing again.
Take the start time from the end time.

guided_steps.pre: Check: over the flat part the distance stayed at
guided_steps.hint: Read the height of the flat line.
guided_steps.done: The distance did not change, so the stop lasted 1 hour.

bronze.display: A car travels 120 km in 3 hours. What is the average speed in km/h?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 km/h. Dividing time by distance (3 ÷ 120 = 0.025) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time.

guided_steps.hint: It is given in the question.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 120 km, so 40 km/h is right.

bronze.display: A cyclist travels at 15 km/h for 2 hours. How far do they go?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time = 15 × 2 = 30 km. Dividing (15 ÷ 2 = 7.5) instead of multiplying is the slip.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time.

guided_steps.hint: It is given in the question.
Two hours at 15 km each hour.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 15 km/h, so 30 km is right.

bronze.display: A bus travels 50 miles in 2.5 hours. What is the speed in mph?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 50 ÷ 2.5 = 20 mph. Dividing time by distance (2.5 ÷ 50 = 0.05) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time.

guided_steps.hint: It is given in the question.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 50 miles, so 20 mph is right.

bronze.display: A conversion graph shows 5 miles ≈ 8 km. Use it to convert 15 miles to kilometres.
bronze.hint: Miles are the bigger unit, so scale up: find the km in 1 mile first.

misconceptions.message: 5 miles is 8 km, so 1 mile is 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 km, and 15 × 1.6 = 24 km. Going the wrong way (15 ÷ 8 × 5 = 9.375) gives fewer km than miles, which is impossible.

guided_steps.say: Miles are bigger than kilometres, so the km number will be larger. Find the km in one mile first.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 15 miles, so 24 km is right.

bronze.display: A runner completes 800 m in 200 seconds. What is their speed in m/s?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 800 ÷ 200 = 4 m/s. Dividing time by distance (200 ÷ 800 = 0.25) is upside down.

guided_steps.say: Speed = distance ÷ time.

guided_steps.hint: It is given in the question.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 800 m, so 4 m/s is right.

bronze.display: A train travels at 60 mph for 1.5 hours. How far does it travel?

misconceptions.message: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 1.5 = 90 miles. Dividing (60 ÷ 1.5 = 40) instead of multiplying is the slip.

guided_steps.say: Distance = speed × time.

guided_steps.hint: It is given in the question.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 60 mph, so 90 miles is right.

silver.display: A car accelerates from 0 to 25 m/s in 5 seconds. What is the acceleration?

misconceptions.message: Acceleration = change in speed ÷ time = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 m/s². Dividing time by the speed change (5 ÷ 25 = 0.2) is upside down.

silver.hint: Acceleration is the gradient: change in speed ÷ time.

guided_steps.say: Acceleration is the gradient of a speed-time graph: change in speed ÷ time.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the speed gain by the time.

guided_steps.done: It reaches the 25 m/s, so 5 m/s² is right.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a car journey. Find the total distance travelled.

misconceptions.message: Split the area: triangle 40, rectangle 80, triangle 20, total 140 m. Treating it all as one rectangle (10 × 20) gives 200, too big.

silver.hint: Split the area into a triangle, a rectangle, then a triangle, and add them.

guided_steps.say: Distance is the area under the line. Split it into a triangle, a rectangle, then a triangle.

guided_steps.pre: Triangle while speeding up (0 to 4 s): ½ × 4 × 20 =
Rectangle at steady speed (4 to 8 s): 4 × 20 =
Triangle while slowing down (8 to 10 s): ½ × 2 × 20 =

guided_steps.done: 140 m over 10 s averages 14 m/s, between 0 and 20, so it is sensible.

silver.display: A car decelerates from 24 m/s to 0 in 3 seconds. What is the deceleration in m/s²?

misconceptions.message: Deceleration = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 m/s². Dividing time by the speed change (3 ÷ 24 = 0.125) is upside down.

silver.hint: Deceleration is the size of the gradient: change in speed ÷ time.

guided_steps.say: Deceleration is the size of the gradient: how fast the speed drops.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the drop by the time.

guided_steps.pre: Check: losing 8 m/s each second for 3 s loses 8 × 3 =
guided_steps.done: That is the full 24 m/s, so 8 m/s² is right.

silver.display: A distance-time graph shows 0 km at t=0 and 90 km at t=1.5 hours. What is the speed?

misconceptions.message: Speed = distance ÷ time = 90 ÷ 1.5 = 60 km/h. Writing 90 gives the distance, not the speed.

silver.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time; read the climb off the graph.

guided_steps.say: Speed on a distance-time graph is distance ÷ time.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 90 km, so 60 km/h is right.

misconceptions.message: £ to € means multiply by 1.15: 200 × 1.15 = €230. Leaving it as 200 forgets to convert.

silver.hint: Convert from pounds to euros by multiplying by the rate 1.15.

guided_steps.say: To go from pounds to euros, multiply by the exchange rate 1.15.

guided_steps.done: It returns the £200, so €230 is right.

silver.display: A speed-time graph shows constant speed of 15 m/s for 8 seconds. What is the distance?

misconceptions.message: The speed is constant, so the area is a rectangle: 8 × 15 = 120 m. Using ½ (as for a triangle) gives 60, which is wrong for a flat line.

silver.hint: A flat speed-time line gives a rectangle: base × height.

guided_steps.say: The line is flat, so the area under it is a rectangle.

guided_steps.done: It returns the constant 15 m/s, so 120 m is right.

silver.display: 8 km ≈ 5 miles. Convert 40 km to miles.

misconceptions.message: 8 km is 5 miles, so 40 ÷ 8 × 5 = 25 miles. Going the wrong way (40 ÷ 5 × 8 = 64) gives more than the km, impossible since miles are the bigger unit.

silver.hint: Kilometres are smaller than miles, so scale down: find the miles in 1 km first.

guided_steps.say: Kilometres are smaller than miles, so the miles number will be smaller. Find the miles in one km first.

guided_steps.done: It returns the 40 km, so 25 miles is right.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Read distance-time graphs and use speed = distance ÷ time with matching units.
problem_bank.silver_description: Read speed-time graphs for acceleration and area, plus unit and currency conversions.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-stage speed-time journeys, reverse area problems, and reading a single graph section.

worked_examples.question: A distance-time graph shows a journey of 80 km in 2 hours. What is the speed?
A speed-time graph shows a car accelerating from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 seconds, then travelling at 20 m/s for 10 seconds. Find the total distance.
A speed-time graph shows a car decelerating from 30 m/s to 0 in 6 seconds. Find the deceleration.

bronze.title: Bronze: speed, distance and time
steps: Speed = distance ÷ time. Rearranged: distance = speed × time, and time = distance ÷ speed.
On a distance-time graph the height is the distance, a flat line means stopped, and a steeper line means faster.
Keep units matched: km with hours gives km/h.

example.question: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. Find its speed.

silver.title: Silver: speed-time graphs and conversions
steps: On a speed-time graph the gradient is the acceleration: change in speed ÷ time.
The area under a speed-time graph is the distance. Split it into triangles and rectangles.
For conversions, scale the right way: miles are bigger than km, and pounds are worth more than euros here.

example.question: A car speeds up from 0 to 18 m/s in 6 s. Find the acceleration.

gold.title: Gold: multi-stage journeys
steps: Break a journey into stages: speeding up, steady, slowing down. Work out each stage on its own.
For total distance, add the area of every stage: two triangles and a rectangle for a trapezium.
To find a missing speed from a known area, write ½ × base × height = area and solve.

example.question: A bus goes 0 to 16 m/s in 4 s, then holds 16 m/s for 6 s. Total distance?

opener.display: The graph shows Maya's drive to her aunt's house and back. Distance from home is up the side, time in hours along the bottom.

steps.pre: How far away is the aunt's house? Read the highest the line reaches:
steps.hint: The line climbs, then flattens. Read that flat height.

steps.pre: Maya rested while the line is flat, from 1 hour to 2 hours. How many hours is that?
steps.hint: Take the start time from the end time of the flat part: 2 − 1.

steps.pre: The whole trip finishes when the line reaches 0 again. At what time, in hours?
steps.hint: Read the time where the line touches the bottom on the right.

steps.say: You just read a distance-time graph by common sense. The height is distance from home, a flat line means not moving, and a steeper slope means going faster. That slope is the speed. Speed-time graphs work the same way, and their area gives the distance. That is the whole of today's lesson.

bronze.display: A van drives 90 km in 2 hours at a steady speed, then carries on for 3 more hours at the same speed. How far does it travel in total?

steps.say: Steady speed means we can find one speed and reuse it for the rest of the trip.

steps.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

steps.pre: At that speed each hour covers
steps.hint: At 45 km/h you go 45 km every hour.
Add the first part to the extra part.
steps.done: Same speed throughout, so the distances just add up. That was the whole point.

silver.display: The speed-time graph shows a motorbike. It speeds up from rest to 16 m/s in 4 s, then holds 16 m/s until 12 s. Find the total distance.

steps.say: On a speed-time graph the area under the line is the distance. Split it into a triangle and a rectangle.

steps.hint: Gradient is change in speed over time.
Area of a triangle is ½ × base × height.
The steady part lasts from 4 s to 12 s, that is 8 s.

steps.done: Area under the graph is the distance. That was the whole point.

gold.display: A tram speeds up from rest to 20 m/s in 4 s, holds 20 m/s for 10 s, then slows to rest in 6 s. Find the total distance.

steps.say: A trapezium splits into two triangles and a rectangle. Find each area, then add.

steps.hint: base × height, over the 10 s at 20 m/s.

steps.done: Every stage's area adds to the total distance. That was the whole point.
